items.content:
Hello, everyone!

Nominations for the Steam Awards 2026 are now open!

In 2026, Palworld finally reached its full release!

Have you ever found yourself thinking something like this while playing Palworld?

"Just five more minutes of exploring."

"Just one more Pal to catch."

"Just a little more work on my base."

And before you know it, hours have flown by...

If you've ever had an experience like this in Palworld, we'd love it if you nominated Palworld for the "Just 5 More Minutes" Award at the Steam Awards 2026!

Nomination Period: November 23–30 (Pacific Time)

We'll keep working to make Palworld the kind of game that makes you think, "Just five more minutes!"

And we hope you're looking forward to our upcoming winter update, v1.1 Side by Side!

The Palworld Development Team

items.title: Get Palworld and 11 other games in Humble's Survival of the Fittest bundle
items.summary: Test your survival skills across diverse challenges with Humble's brand-new Survival of the Fittest game bundle!
items.content:
Humble has launched another game bundle, this time focusing on survival experiences that put players in some particularly hostile environments. The Survival of the Fittest Bundle brings together 12 items across several genres, covering everything from underwater exploration and vehicle building to creature collecting and vampire-themed action. Buyers can choose between two pricing tiers, depending on how much of the collection they want.

The entry-level option costs $15 (€13 / £11) and includes 10 items. One of its biggest attractions is Subnautica: Below Zero , which takes players back to the alien planet 4546B. Following the disappearance of your sister, you'll explore its frozen regions, dive beneath vast sheets of ice, and investigate the mysteries hidden beneath the ocean's surface. Its striking underwater environments offer plenty of beauty, but the dangers lurking below make every expedition a potential fight for survival.

Another highlight is Mr. Prepper , a crafting-focused survival game built around the threat of an impending nuclear war. Players must prepare for disaster while living under an authoritarian government, gathering resources and constructing an underground shelter. The looming catastrophe and constant pressure to stay ahead of the authorities give the experience a different twist compared with more traditional survival games.

Those willing to spend more can opt for the $25 tier (€22 / £19), which adds two more games to complete the 12-item collection.

The first is Palworld , a creature-collecting adventure that combines colorful exploration with surprisingly demanding survival and management mechanics. Players can capture and befriend Pals, take them into battle, and assign them various jobs around their bases. Building a thriving operation requires more than simply collecting creatures, with automation and resource production playing an important role.

The other major addition is V Rising , which puts players in the role of a newly awakened vampire. Surviving means hunting for blood, avoiding deadly sunlight, and gradually rebuilding a castle worthy of a vampire lord. As you defeat increasingly powerful enemies and expand your influence, your modest hideout can eventually become a formidable fortress.

As usual, you’ll find the complete lineup of Humble’s Survival of the Fittest Bundle over Humble’s official site. For another collection aimed at PC gaming enthusiasts, Fanatical is also offering its separate Play on the Go Elite Collection , featuring 20 Steam games suited to handheld gaming devices.

The Humble Survival of the Fittest Bundle is available through Humble's official store until December 8. Buyers should also keep the redemption deadline in mind, as all included game keys must be activated by June 5, 2027. As always, if you’re looking to get the most value from your gaming budget, be sure to browse our dedicated deals hub for the latest offers.

A writer, and a full-time Tetris min-maxing player. Do you know that rhythm games are a form of human benchmarking?

items.title: Palworld is not Pokémon … and that’s the point
items.summary: While most people spent their summer break finding ways to escape the heat, I spent mine building bases, catching creatures and exploring a world that kept me coming back every single day and night. Over 200 hours later, Palworld has become my most played game in my Steam library. It may look like Pokémon at...
items.content:
While most people spent their summer break finding ways to escape the heat, I spent mine building bases, catching creatures and exploring a world that kept me coming back every single day and night.

Over 200 hours later, Palworld has become my most played game in my Steam library. It may look like Pokémon at first glance, but there is so much more to it beyond catching creatures.

The big selling point for both games is running around a world and capturing creatures of different species. Palworld even has its own ball throwing mechanic similar to Pokémon; but after investing an entire summer into the game, calling Palworld “Pokémon with guns” is nothing more than a weak analogy.

The biggest difference is how the aspect of creature collecting is used in the games.

In Pokémon, catching creatures is at the forefront of the game. One of the main goals is to capture every single Pokémon and complete the pokedex, hence the slogan “Gotta catch ‘em all,” whereas Palworld is a survival game first and a creature collecting game second.

In Palworld, catching a new creature, or Pal, as it’s called in the game, can mean so much more than just having a new fighter on your team.

Pals can be used to help you build up your base by collecting resources, planting crops, transporting materials and manufacturing items. Some Pals are great for fighting and exploring, while others are essential for upgrading your base and completing mundane tasks within the game.

Instead of just seeing which creatures are the strongest in the game, Palworld drives you to find which pals are best for your overall survival.

I wasn’t just collecting Pals for the sake of completing a collection; I was catching Pals that would benefit me best for specific needs. Chikipi was never going to be strong enough to take on a boss battle, but it was great for producing essential food items at the base so my character and Pals wouldn’t starve and I wouldn’t have to waste precious time looking for food.

This is what makes Palworld so different from Pokémon. The Pals are much more than just tools for combat, and make the game feel less like a turn-based fighting game and more like an open world survival.

Pokémon shows their creatures as friends and partners, while Palworld doesn’t share that sentiment. Pals can fight, work, hunt or even become resources for survival. The game doesn’t hold back in putting you in a world where survival takes priority over being nice.

It also gives you so much freedom. Pokémon has a streamlined path to it. Explore an area, catch Pokémon, battle trainers, get badges and move on to the next gym to eventually beat the elite four and become the new champion. Palworld gives you a world and lets you decide what you want to do with it.

With this freedom, you can come back to it and spend each session doing something different. I could log in one day and spend it working on my base, and the next day spend it exploring a new area or progressing in the story.

These aspects are what make the comparison of these games so misleading.

Palworld CEO wants to bring the game to Switch 2 despite ongoing Nintendo lawsuit
items.summary: Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe wants to discuss bringing Palworld to Nintendo Switch 2, despite the studio
items.content:
Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe wants to discuss bringing Palworld to Nintendo Switch 2, despite the studio's ongoing patent lawsuit with Nintendo.

VIEW GALLERY - 3 Three armed Pals in Palworld, whose developer says it would welcome talks about bringing the game to Nintendo Switch 2 despite its ongoing lawsuit with Nintendo. (Image: Pocketpair) Hassam Nasir Senior Tech Reporter Published Oct 28, 2026 5:04 PM CDT 1 minute & 15 seconds read time What you need to know Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe says the studio would like to discuss bringing Palworld to Nintendo Switch 2, which he praised as a strong platform. The patent lawsuit with Nintendo remains active, making a port difficult to envision for now.

As an Amazon Associate, we earn from qualifying purchases. TweakTown may also earn commissions from other affiliate partners at no extra cost to you.

Palworld has spent the last two years in a courtroom with Nintendo , but its developer still wants to bring the game to Nintendo's console.

Go ad-free with Supporter See plans and prices

Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe told VGC that bringing Palworld to the Switch 2 is "of course" something the studio wants, calling the console "a really amazing platform, not just for games globally, but especially here in Japan and for the Japanese games industry."

If there's ever a future where we have the opportunity to discuss or consider bringing Palworld to the Switch platform in some way, then we'd love to have those conversations.

Mizobe did not discuss the lawsuit itself, since it is ongoing.

Back in 2024, Mizobe said a Switch version was unlikely because of the original console's limits. In March 2025, Pocketpair communications director John Buckley told IGN that Palworld is "a beefy game" that would not run on the original Switch, but that a Switch 2 port was "100% worth considering" once the specs were known. Now that the hardware is out and handling plenty of current-gen games, the answer is a little more direct.

3 A Palworld player faces a large pink creature in a rocky pool; Pocketpair's CEO says he would welcome talks about bringing the game to Switch 2. (Image: Pocketpair) VIEW GALLERY - 3 IMAGES Nintendo filed its patent infringement lawsuit in September 2024, then narrowed it in November 2025 to focus on older versions of the game, after Pocketpair patched out the contested mechanics, including throwing a Pal Sphere to summon a Pal and Pal-based gliding. The case remains active.

The Tokyo District Court is expected to share its preliminary view on November 9, which could say a lot about how things move from here. Another detail worth noting: the Japanese Patent Office rejected Nintendo's patent application for creature-capture mechanics in October 2025. However, that is a separate matter from the lawsuit.

3 Riders fly across Palworld’s landscape in gameplay footage as Pocketpair’s CEO expresses interest in discussing a Switch 2 version despite the ongoing Nintendo lawsuit. (Image: Pocketpair) Realistically, it is hard to picture a Palworld port reaching the Switch 2 while the two companies are still suing each other. After all, publishing on a platform means working with the platform holder.

The Sunlit Isle (405, -483) Pros: Several crude oil nodes, easy to defend during raids Cons: No nearby ore Closest teleport: Sunlit Isle It's not the best spot for ore or stone, but the Sunlit Isle just east of Palworld's starting area makes early game crude oil farming a breeze with six nodes scattered across the land. ・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Pals in The World Tree area.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Teafant Spring.

・Adjusted the work amount required to craft the Ancient Armor series.

・Doubled the amount of Fiber obtained from trees.

▼Bases and Missions

・Reduced the building costs of the Crude Oil Extractor, High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor, and Large Power Generator.

・Increased the crude oil production speed of the Crude Oil Extractor and High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

・The base mission that requires building a Crude Oil Extractor can now also be progressed by building a High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

▼Server Settings

・Added a server setting (bAllowEnemyCampSpawnNearBaseCamp) that disables the suppression of enemy camp spawns near player base camps.

\

▼Graphics and Display

・Adjusted the boundary display in some areas to make it easier to see from a distance.

・Improved the display quality of some objects in dungeons.

▼Sound

・Added a sound effect when using World Tree Holy Water.

\

▼Crashes and Progression Blockers

・Fixed an issue where the mission could become impossible to progress if the barrier was removed before accepting the main mission in Sunreach.

▼Multiplayer and Co-op

・Fixed an issue in co-op where lighting on the client side could display incorrectly after cutscenes or the ending played.

・Fixed an issue in co-op where some scenes could stutter during the cutscene that plays when entering The World Tree.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Fast Travel could activate unintentionally during Tower Boss battles.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Pals could appear to vibrate rapidly on the client screen.

▼Pals and NPCs

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop fighting.

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop helping with base work.

・Fixed an issue in multiplayer where, when the Partner Skill of Orserk or certain other Pals activated, the effect display could fail to update correctly, making it appear as though the skill had not activated.

・Fixed an issue where Alpha Surfent would not produce Leather when assigned to a Ranch.

▼Battles and Bosses

・Fixed an issue where some raid boss battles could fail to progress as intended.

・Fixed an issue where the wave effect and actual damage range did not match for some of Panthalus's attacks.

▼Bases and Building

・Fixed an issue where the placement detection for stairs and slanted roofs could fail to match their actual shape.

・Fixed an issue where stairs could not be placed correctly on the sides of foundations or roofs.

▼Items and Rewards

・Fixed an issue where the reward settings for the normal Moon Lord battle and the Ultra Raid Boss battle had not been updated to the intended settings.

・Fixed an issue where items could duplicate when performing certain actions.

・Fixed an issue where, when Katress's Partner Skill activated, switching spheres while riding could allow the player to obtain a different type of sphere.

・Fixed an issue where the World Tree Holy Water effect did not display correctly on the Pal being ridden when using World Tree Holy Water while riding.

・Fixed an issue where, after the World Tree Holy Water effect ended, riding a Pal would cause the World Tree Holy Water aura to reappear and not disappear when approaching trees in The World Tree area.

・Fixed an issue where an unintended reward was set for the desert expedition.

・Fixed an issue where the Dark Skill Fruit: Psycho Gravity did not appear on the item search screen.

・Fixed a bug where the firing interval was not set for sphere launchers

▼UI, Display, and Text

・Fixed an issue where resolution settings would not apply correctly in fullscreen mode.

・Fixed an issue where, after switching window mode with F11 / Alt+Enter, the game could unintentionally return to fullscreen mode after loading.

・Fixed an issue where, if certain effects were on screen while aiming, the entire screen could become blurred.

▼Sound

・Fixed an issue where the water sound effect could fail to play at Teafant Spring.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where the BGM for Attack Choppers triggered by other players could play even from far away.

・Adjusted the BGM playback range for Attack Choppers so that it plays correctly for players who are Wanted.

・Fixed an issue where unintended footstep sounds could play when walking on furniture or facilities.

▼Controls

・Fixed an issue where, after changing the key assignment for ""Attack that enemy!"" in Controls, selecting ""Restore to Default"" would not restore the default setting.

・Fixed an issue where settings could be applied unintentionally when interacting with the change confirmation dialog and duplicate key warning in Controls.

▼Map and Exploration

・Fixed an issue where a beach-like display could remain on the water surface after Fast Traveling to an offshore base.

items.title: This New Survival Game Finally Clicked with Me, and I'm Never Looking Back
items.summary: Palworld 1.0 does a great job of easing you into its many complex systems.
items.content:
Survival games have been wildly popular for years now. I’ve dabbled here and there to see what the fuss is about, but I’ve always fallen off after a few hours. Usually, I get tangled up in one meagerly explained system after another until I lose track of what I’m supposed to do, and my time with the game peters out.

When Palworld 1.0 came out to rave reviews , I figured I’d give the genre another shot – and I’m glad I did. Palworld’s gradual, newbie-friendly onboarding helped me see what a whole lot of people have loved about survival games all along. Palworld made me a believer.

I’m glad I came in at the 1.0 mark, because I’ve heard Palworld had a much steeper learning curve out of the gate. But now, new players start with a series of missions designed to guide you through the game’s numerous systems . You learn how to punch trees to get wood to create a crafting bench. You learn how to make a club you can use to beat some Pals to death (it’s a dog-eat-dog world out there) to get wool. You then use that wool to make clothes. You set up a camp. You build a house. You activate a teleporter and explore deeper into the game world.

Before long, you’re gliding off cliffs Zelda-style before whomping on every Pal you see to catch them in spheres to put them to work. You can deploy them at your camp, ride them , or have them fight by your side to take on big roaming Pals and towering bosses . It’s a blast. And there’s no way I would have stuck with it if it hadn’t held my hand and eased me into the systems that make up the game.

I still have a long way to go, because I was nowhere near powerful enough to defeat the first boss solo. But those early missions gave me a much-needed handle on what else I can spend my time doing as I level up enough to become a threat. There's a vast world out there I can keep exploring, all while catching Pals and building up my base. I’m having a blast doing it.

Palworld’s 1.0 is available on Steam , Xbox , and PS5 . It costs $29.99, but you can save a few bucks on a Steam copy at Fanatical , which is currently running its summer sale .

Chris Reed is a commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .
